clue.text: Doubly safe option, girdle and stays?

parts.note: a girdle is a belt worn round the waist
taken as written
stays here are braces, things that hold trousers up

explanation.surface: A question about underwear that both holds in and holds up, as a way of being extra careful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the idiom for taking two precautions where one would do, as with a man who wears both a waist strap and shoulder straps to keep his trousers up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes taking two safeguards at once, a doubled precaution against failure.

clue.text: Don't forgive churlish type, a rugged criminal

parts.note: a bear is a rude, grumpy person
taken as written

indicators.note: criminal suggests the word rugged is corrupted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A loutish, rough-looking crook who will not forgive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' turns RUGGED into GRUDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing resentment against someone, rather than pardoning them, is to refuse forgiveness.

clue.text: Sign made by one supporter after end of final

indicators.note: after means the next pieces follow that letter
end of means just the closing letter of the word final

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a bra is an undergarment that supports

explanation.surface: A star sign is created by a single fan once the final is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' looks like a fan, fitting a final, but it is a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Divine, a doctor meeting sailor at sea

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of sailor are mixed up

explanation.surface: A heavenly encounter between a physician and a seaman on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the sailor's picture but signals that SAILOR becomes ROSIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, so something ambrosial is divinely delicious.

clue.text: Democrat, in league, moved slowly

parts.note: allied means joined in league with others

explanation.surface: A Democrat politician, hand in glove with others, took his time.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to dawdle or loiter, so dallied means proceeded slowly.

clue.text: Puzzle over old car

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as over does in arguing over something
bus is dated slang for a motor car

explanation.surface: Scratching one's head over a vintage car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' sounds like puzzling over something, but it gives RE, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Not entirely risky engaging horse for coach

indicators.note: engaging means the shortened word takes the horse inside it
not entirely means the final letter of the word for risky is dropped

parts.note: chancy means risky
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A slightly dangerous plan to harness a horse to a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims the final letter of the synonym for risky; 'engaging' sounds like charming but means holding the horse inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Son, notice, is blue

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A father reports that his son is feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is a common idiom for being unhappy or low in spirits.

clue.text: Spike first of barrels at back of pub

indicators.note: at back of places the single letter after the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking room

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the word barrels is used

explanation.surface: Something sharp sticks out from behind the pub where the barrels are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a sharp backward-pointing spike, as on a fish hook or wire.

clue.text: On which people may appear larger than life, by the way?

definitions.text: On which people may appear larger than life, by the way?

parts.words: On which people may appear larger than life, by the way?
parts.note: giant posters stand by the roadside, literally by the way, showing faces many times life size

explanation.surface: An offhand question about where people look bigger than they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like a conversational aside, but it means beside the road, where large advertising hoardings stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadside advertising hoardings show people's pictures far larger than life size, so they fit the description.

clue.text: A dandy in a vehicle on entering motorway

indicators.note: entering means the following pieces go inside the motorway's abbreviation

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI in crosswords
taken as written
a car is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fop in a car is joining the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a motorway running north from London; crosswords write its name as MI. 'A' in the surface looks like part of the definition but supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In eighteenth-century Britain a macaroni was a fashionable young man affecting Continental styles, a fop or dandy.

clue.text: Agent, ringing down, is irritable

indicators.note: ringing means the agent's word encircles the other piece

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
nap is the soft downy surface of cloth

explanation.surface: A spy, phoning in a depressed mood, snaps at people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads as sad, but it is the soft fuzz on fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snappy is short-tempered and quick to speak sharply, which is irritable.

clue.text: Fiend, one cutting up man, badly, causes uproar

indicators.note: cutting means the fiend and one are put into the rearranged letters
badly means the letters of up man are disordered

parts.note: a demon is a fiend
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A devil attacking someone viciously creates a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reads as part of 'cutting up', but it joins MAN as the anagram fodder, made PANUM; DEMONI goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandemonium is wild and noisy disorder, chaos or uproar.

clue.text: A ground squirrel with a plain tail

parts.note: a prairie is a plain, the grassland of North America
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: Describing a small rodent whose tail is undecorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail' looks like a noun for the squirrel's tail but is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing North American rodent belongs to the squirrel family and lives on the ground in colonies.

clue.text: I mixed drink with style, here in London

parts.note: taken as written
a sling is a mixed drink, such as the gin sling
ton is fashionable style

explanation.surface: Someone sips a cocktail with flair in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like an anagram signal but just describes the cocktail. TON, fashion, is an old word from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a district of north London, so the clue's place phrase points to it.

clue.text: Crack crackers and become very angry

parts.note: a crack at something is a go, an attempt
crackers and bananas both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Someone snaps open Christmas novelties and flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack crackers' suggests pulling Christmas crackers; it gives GO plus BANANAS, which means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bananas is slang for becoming wildly angry or excited.

clue.text: Composer from department in NE France, not married

indicators.note: not means the letter for married is removed from the department's name

parts.note: the Marne is a French administrative department in the north-east

explanation.surface: A bachelor composer who comes from a region of north-east France.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was the eighteenth-century English composer of Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was an English composer, best known for Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Superstar, one seen with dummy, endlessly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the doll word is removed

parts.note: a doll is a model figure, a dummy

explanation.surface: A celebrity is forever photographed with a ventriloquist's puppet.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a hugely admired star, worshipped by fans as a superstar.

clue.text: American footballer in row with supporter

parts.note: a line is a row
a backer is one who supports

explanation.surface: A gridiron player gets into a quarrel with a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football this defensive player stands behind the line of scrimmage.

clue.text: On about b— stubborn person over in plant

indicators.note: over means the whole assembled string is turned round
about means the word on goes around the next pieces

parts.note: taken as written
the bare letter b, coyly given as if for a swear word
a mule is an obstinate person

explanation.surface: Someone muttering a curse about an obstinate gardener in a plant bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'b—' looks like a censored expletive; it is just the letter. 'About' wraps, then 'over' turns the whole string, so the plant's name reads backwards from the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the lotus, an aquatic plant.

clue.text: That girl treated Ian for a rupture

parts.note: her refers to that girl

indicators.note: treated means the name Ian is reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman gave Ian medical care for his torn tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' looks medical, fitting the scene, but signals a rearrangement of IAN to NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is a rupture, the protrusion of an organ through the wall containing it.

clue.text: Farewell to the Parisian about to depart

definitions.meaning: a farewell is a word of parting

definitions.text: to the Parisian about to depart
definitions.meaning: what one says in French to someone leaving, a goodbye to God's keeping

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the word a French speaker says to a departing friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French word of parting, used in English for goodbye.

clue.text: The Outsider, lengthy picture

parts.note: lengthy means long
a shot is a photograph or picture

explanation.surface: A lengthy film adaptation of the novel The Outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics suggest a book title (Camus's novel), but the definition is simply an outsider in a race or contest.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlikely winner, a rank outsider in a race, is called this in betting.

clue.text: Novel about 7, headless ghost

indicators.note: about means the novel's title goes around the shortened piece

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the answer to 7 down goes

parts.note: the clue number points to the answer at 7 down, a word for blue

explanation.surface: A novel concerning a melancholy ghost that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is a cross-reference to the answer at 7 down; 'headless' drops its first letter, and 'about' puts the remainder inside the Haggard title.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost or spirit of the dead.

clue.text: Film an Oz character capturing husband

indicators.note: capturing means the Oz character's name holds the husband letter inside

parts.note: the Tin Man is a character in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A film in which a Wizard of Oz figure seizes a married man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thin Man is a 1934 detective film based on Dashiell Hammett's novel.

clue.text: Ben injured, losing foot

indicators.note: losing foot means the bottom letter of the down entry is removed

parts.note: hurt means injured

explanation.surface: Ben has been hurt and has lost a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the answer completes the name Ben-Hur, the chariot-racing hero of Lew Wallace's novel and the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben-Hur is the title hero of Lew Wallace's novel, so the name follows Ben.

clue.text: A song from Callas needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the first letter of the singer's forename goes

parts.note: Maria Callas was the famous opera soprano

explanation.surface: A song by Callas, a singer so famous she needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' sounds like praise of the famous diva but means dropping her name's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, the kind Callas sang.

clue.text: To our fans, possibly, side became weary

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of to our fans could be arranged another way

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A football team flagged late on, as it might say to its supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns TO OUR FANS into RANOUTOFS.
explanation.definitionFit: To run out of steam is an idiom for losing energy and becoming tired.
